title: Signals in everyday conversation
objectives: Match six client behaviours to their likely biases.
Listen for biases in what clients say, before advising.
body_md:
Biases show up in what clients say and do, so the first skill is listening for them. Wants to stop SIPs after a fall: loss aversion. Asks for “the fund everyone is buying”: herd / FOMO. Quotes last year's return as the reason to invest: recency bias. Waits to “break even” before selling: anchoring. Checks the app daily and calls after every dip: myopic loss aversion. Keeps money idle in savings “for now”: status quo / inertia.

| Client behaviour | Likely bias |
| --- | --- |
| Wants to stop SIPs after a fall | Loss aversion |
| Asks for "the fund everyone is buying" | Herd / FOMO |
| Quotes last year's return as the reason to invest | Recency bias |
| Waits to "break even" before selling | Anchoring |
| Checks the app daily and calls after every dip | Myopic loss aversion |
| Keeps money idle in savings "for now" | Status quo / inertia |
example: “Everyone is buying small-caps” → herd/FOMO: check fit with allocation first, before discussing the fund.
say: Listen for the bias in what the client says before advising.
“The fund everyone is buying” is a herd signal, not a recommendation.
never: Client behaviour is random and meaningless.
Quote last year's return as the reason to invest.

check.q: "Everyone in my WhatsApp group is buying this small-cap fund." Which bias?
check.why: Herd / FOMO. Following the crowd, often after a rally.

check.q: "I check my portfolio every day and it stresses me." Which bias?
check.why: Myopic loss aversion. Frequent checking makes normal swings feel like losses.

check.q: A client checks the app daily and calls after every dip. Which bias?
check.why: Checks the app daily and calls after every dip: myopic loss aversion.
